notes: Access: tier-1 HTTP only, no block encountered (robots.txt generic Allow:/, no Claude disallow). Site is a Nuxt/Vue SPA over a headless WordPress 'trouble' REST backend (wp.andtradition.com/wp-json/trouble/*, openly readable, confirmed by prior pass). Checked exhaustively: (1) trouble/taxonomy - the full ~175-term product taxonomy dump that is the site's own source for the frontend's '/products?type=<slug>' filter; scanned every term name for Bestseller/Best Selling/Best-Selling/Top Seller/Popular/Favorite/Trending (English) equivalents - none exist. (2) trouble/routes - the site's full 628-URL prerender/route manifest; none of /bestsellers, /best-sellers, /best-selling, /top-sellers, /popular, /customer-favorites (or any keyword match for best|top-sell|popular|favourite|trend) is a registered route. (3) trouble/frontpage (homepage ACF modules) - no bestseller-themed section or link. (4) Per assignment hint, checked the 'Professionals' B2B/trade page (wp-json trouble/post?slug=professionals) since some Danish design brands gate merchandising pages behind a trade login: it is a public, non-password-protected (acf.password_protect=false) info page about contract/trade services with no login gate and no bestseller link. Candidate URLs https://www.andtradition.com/bestsellers and /best-sellers return HTTP 200 but render the generic '&Tradition' shell <title> (not the '&Tradition — Products' title every real /products?type=X page carries, verified against both a known-valid type and a deliberately-invalid type) and are absent from the 628-route manifest - i.e. they are unmatched/fallback routes, not real pages. The site's own search API (trouble/search) was also tried (sale/outlet/bestseller/best seller/new arrivals/sample sale/clearance) but returns an identical default 'Portraits of Living' result for every query - a known false-absence trap per project notes, so it was not relied upon; taxonomy + full route-manifest enumeration were used instead as the authoritative absence proof. Conclusion: no genuine Bestsellers-type merchandising PLP exists on this site.
